en: The Ritual for Empowerment.
Oṃ, homage to the glorious Vajrasattva!

Therein, having instructed one, two, or many disciples who have completed the mandala ritual—having placed their knees upon the ground with their hands joined in a gesture of reverence (*añjali*) holding flowers—one should cause them to hear: "This entry into the mandala is not for the sake of prosperity in this world alone, nor even for the sake of prosperity in the next world; rather, it must be performed for the sake of attaining the perfection of the three bodies (*trikāya*) of the Tathāgata. If that is done, both forms of prosperity will be accomplished. Then, [the master] visualizes [the disciple's essence] entering through his own mouth, emerging from the *vajra*, and entering the mouths of the Tathāgatas of Wisdom who reside within the lotuses at the hearts [of the deities]. These Tathāgatas, drawn by the rays of light from the seed-syllable at the heart, become liquefied and consecrate [the disciple]. Having thus meditated, he should seat [the disciple] at the eastern gate of the mandala and have him request entry.
From the ocean of existence, which is terrifying with its crocodiles of death, birth, old age, and disease, you alone are my savior; you are my teacher, the Great Hero.
I desire, O Great Lord, this firm path of great awakening;
grant me the commitment (samaya) and the reality (tattva), and grant me the spirit of awakening (bodhicitta).
Grant me the three refuges: the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha;
O Protector, lead me into the supreme city of great liberation.
Thus he recited: "Come, child, I shall teach you the method of the mantra practice of the Mahāyāna; for you are a worthy vessel for the Great Way."
The Buddhas, arisen throughout the three times, possess the vajras of body, speech, and mind;
they have attained incomparable gnosis through the cultivation of vajra mantras.
By means of this incomparable application of mantra,
the great and most terrible army of Māra was shattered by the excellent ones, such as the Lion of the Śākyas.
Having conformed to worldly convention and set the wheel in motion, they have attained liberation;
therefore, my son, apply your mind to this for the sake of attaining omniscience.
Having thus exhorted [the practitioner] with this recitation, one should then say: "The Three Jewels are my refuge; I confess all [my misdeeds];
I rejoice in the merit of the world; and my mind is set upon the awakening of a Buddha."
Thus one should cause [the disciple] to recite three times. This is the general vow.
Having bestowed the irreversible consecration in the mandala, O Lord, speak to me!
The reality of the wheel and the deity, and the preparatory rites for the preceptor.
"The commitment of all Buddhas, the supreme secret vow—may I always be the preceptor for the sake of accomplishing the welfare of all sentient beings. Thus it is said.

Having specifically performed the formal request, one should cause the generation of the thought of awakening (*bodhicitta*) to be made: "May all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas attend to me! I, named so-and-so, from this moment until I am seated at the seat of awakening (*bodhimaṇḍa*)," [I shall maintain the thought of awakening].
I generate the supreme, unsurpassed mind of awakening,
just as the protectors of the three times have made their firm resolve for perfect enlightenment.
I firmly undertake the threefold training in ethical discipline, the gathering of virtuous qualities,
and the ethical discipline of acting for the benefit of sentient beings.
From this day forward, I shall undertake the vow born of the yoga of the Buddha, toward the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha— the unsurpassed, supreme Triple Gem.
I accept the vajra, the bell, and the mudrā according to reality;
and I shall accept the master in the exalted assembly of the Great Vajra Family.
I shall bestow the fourfold gift six times every day,
in a noble family of great jewels, at a fitting and delightful time.
I accept the True Dharma, both external and secret, belonging to the three wombs;
within the pure Mahāpadma family, which is the source of great awakening,
I accept from all sides the vow conjoined with everything.
In accordance with my ability, through this great rite for the exaltation of the Kula,
I generate the supreme, unsurpassed mind of awakening (bodhicitta).
Having taken the complete vow for the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings,
I shall ferry across those who have not crossed over, and I shall liberate those who are not liberated.

"Those who have not found rest, I shall cause to find rest; I shall establish all sentient beings in nirvāṇa. Reciting this, one should then protect them with the Amṛtakuṇḍalī mantra. One should visualize the syllables *HŪṂ*, *ĀḤ*, and *OṂ*—black, red, and white—resting upon a sun, a sun, and a moon, respectively, atop a vajra, a lotus, and a wheel at their hearts, throats, and heads. Then, having performed the invitation (*ākarṣaṇa*) and offered water for the feet (*pādya*) and so forth, one should perform the empowerment of the three bodies (*trikāyādhiṣṭhāna*): offering a flower on the head, incense before [the face], a lamp at the heart, and perfume at the heart. Following that, recite *OṂ VAJRAHĀRĀ HAṂ 3*. This is the casting of the tooth-stick (*dantakāṣṭha*). ||1||

When [the vessel] falls facing east, north, west, south, upward, or downward, there are respectively the accomplishments (*siddhi*) of pacifying (*śāntika*), enriching (*pauṣṭika*), magnetizing (*vaśya*), malevolent rites (*abhicāra*), mastery of the sciences (*vidyādhara*), and the underworld (*pātāla*). Thereafter, one should cause [the disciple] to drink three mouthfuls of scented water with the weapon-mantra: *Oṃ hrīḥ, O pure Dharma, wash away all sins, purify [me], remove all conceptual constructions, hūṃ*. With the mantra *Hūṃ jaṃ*, [one ties] a red thread [around the wrist]. With the mantra *Iti buddhamaitrī rakṣa rakṣa sarvān svāhā*, [one performs] the protection circle (*rakṣā-cakra*).
Whatever evil was previously committed over many millions of eons—
Indeed, all that goes to destruction upon seeing such a mandala.
The source of all suffering, namely miserable rebirth,
is utterly destroyed for those whose minds are supremely pure regarding this excellent conduct.
Today, O great-souled ones, you have obtained incomparable gains,
in that you have been [established] here in this teaching by all the Jinas together with their sons.
"You are all embraced by the great-souled ones as they attain victory;
therefore, you shall indeed be well-born in the Mahāyāna."
This is the glorious, supreme path, the great success of the Mahāyāna.
By means of which you, when departing, shall become Tathāgatas.
Having thus caused [them] to hear.

HŪṂ: Having spread out *kuśa* grass for the sake of a bed; DHĪḤ: having offered a goad born from the syllable DHĪḤ; one should give it with the mantra: OṂ VAJRĪ TĪKṢṆADHĀM. Having recited the Kuṇḍalī-mantra for the purpose of its recitation, one should establish it.
This is the procedure for the preliminary consecration (*adhivāsana*) of the disciple. ||2||

At the time of entering the maṇḍala house: Oṃ, enter, O Blessed One, the city of liberation, which bestows all accomplishments and happiness, for the sake of attaining the supreme, most excellent bliss! Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! It is accomplished by those who are inspired. Having entered and circumambulated, one should approach the form of the Lord of the Mandala at the western and other doors: Oṃ, open the vajra-gate; enter the samaya! Hūṃ! Oṃ, with a mind intent on supreme bliss, I bow to the Blessed One with graceful, playful, and smiling gestures! Jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ! Hiḥ hiḥ hiḥ hiḥ hiḥ hiḥ! Accept this handful of flowers! With "Hoḥ," when the flower garland has been cast, one should perform the consecration of truth (satyādhiṣṭhāna).
Because he is characterized by the arising of space, he is supreme, without beginning or end;
he is the Great Being composed of the great vajra—Akṣobhyavajra and the others—attained by me.
The supreme sovereign of all great accomplishments, the presiding deity of lordship,
the king who holds all vajras— may that Perfected One, the Supreme Immutable, grant me success.
You are faultless and eternal, the one who inspires passion for all passions;
O Blessed One, in reality, you are established as the Great Passion and the Great Joy.
The Tathāgata, who is utterly pure, the foremost of phenomena, and liberated from the beginning;
the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, whose self is all-pervading, is renowned to me.
By means of the supreme mudrā of sovereignty, which is the highest of all great accomplishments,
O Great Vajra of Perfection, through your immense excellence, may I become like Vajragarbha.
Pervading the minds of all sentient beings, abiding in the hearts of all sentient beings,
he is indeed the father of all sentient beings, the supreme object of desire for those who hold the foremost commitments.
By that truth through which perception is the maṇḍala whose nature is wisdom and skillful means,
by that truth, O Protector, fulfill my desires.
All phenomena are like reflections: transparent, pure, and unclouded;
they are ungraspable and inexpressible, yet arise from causes and karma.
By this truth— that [the mandala] has emerged from the reality of suchness— may all disciples, free from defilement, clearly behold the reflection of the mandala.
Thus reciting: The Ritual for the Entrance of the Preceptor. ||3||

Then, having emerged from the mandala house, [one performs] the offering for the disciples' mandala circle and the *bali* offering. Next is the visualization (*bhāvanā*): one visualizes the disciple—who has offered the ritual fee (*dakṣiṇā*)—in the form of Vairocana or as the Lord of the Mandala (*cakrādhipa*). He is sprinkled with water from the *sarvakarmika* vase. His body is radiant with rays of light emanating from the forms of a black *HŪṂ*, a red *ĀḤ*, and a white *OṂ*, which are placed upon sun and moon discs atop the vajra, lotus, and wheel at his heart, throat, and head. Having uttered "HŪṂ," [one performs] the summoning and the offering of water for the feet (*pādya*), and so forth. With the mantra *NIVANCIṆI HŪṂ ĀḤ OṂ*, [one performs] the empowerment of the three bodies (*trikāyādhiṣṭhāna*) using the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) and a cloth over the head.

Oṃ, may the ocean-like clouds of offerings of garments, the ornaments of the unsurpassed awakening of all Tathāgatas, radiate forth; at the time [of this rite], hūṃ! La 3! Adhiṣṭhāna! Oṃ vajra rakṣa haṃ! Go! Oṃ vajroṣṇīṣa hūṃ phaṭ! [This is for] the head-wrap. Oṃ vajrabandha varamānaya hūṃ! [This is for] the blindfold. Āḥ khaṃ vīra hūṃ! [The disciple] takes the flower garland. Then, the curtain should be drawn aside. "Who are you, O lover of pleasure? he asks. He should reply: "I am Subhaga, O Great Bliss! Then, making him recite "Oṃ, I generate the mind of all yoga," he should cause him to generate the *bodhicitta*.

Reciting: *oṃ surate samayas tvaṃ hoḥ siddhya vajra yathāsukhaṃ*, while holding the vajra to the heart; having said, "Today you shall be empowered by all the Tathāgatas, and this supreme secret maṇḍala of all the Tathāgatas must not be spoken of to one who has not entered it, nor should it be revealed to one who lacks faith," and reciting *oṃ āḥ yamāntakṛta hūṃ* while drawing [the disciple] in; then, with *āḥ khaṃ vīra hūṃ*, having caused him to enter within the curtain; and while reciting *mahāratasudṛḍhasutoṣyasusukho vajrasattvādyasiddhaya māṃ*, he circumambulates [the maṇḍala] clockwise and stands at the eastern gate of the maṇḍala with palms joined, [saying]: *oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjopasthānāyātmānaṃ niryātayāmi sarvatathāgatavajrasattvādhiṣṭha mām ||1||* "I offer myself for the service and worship of all the Tathāgatas; may all the Tathāgatas, Vajrasattva, and the rest empower me! ||1||

Oṃ, I offer myself for the service and worship of all Buddhas; O Vajravairocana of all Tathāgatas, empower me! Thus, at the south. (2) Oṃ, I offer myself for the empowerment through the worship of all Tathāgatas; O Vajraratna of all Tathāgatas, consecrate me! At the west. (3) Oṃ, I offer myself for the initiation of the worship of all Tathāgatas; O Vajradharma of all Tathāgatas, set me in motion! At the north. (4) Oṃ, I offer myself for the ritual activity of the worship of all Tathāgatas; O Vajrakarma of all Tathāgatas, perform your work upon me! (5) Again, at the eastern gate: Oṃ, I offer myself for the service of the Guru’s feet; [Oṃ], I offer myself for the sake of protecting all sentient beings. Thus is the fivefold prostration. (4)

"Therefore, today you have entered the family of all the Tathāgatas; thus, I shall generate in you the vajra-wisdom (*vajrajñāna*), by which wisdom you will attain even the accomplishments (*siddhi*) of all the Tathāgatas, let alone other accomplishments. You must not speak of this before anyone who has not seen the maṇḍala, lest your samaya be violated. Having said this, he places the vajra on [the disciple's] head and, sounding the bell, makes him hear: "This is your samaya; the vajra shall split your head if you speak of this to anyone. Then, placing the vajra at his heart:
Oṃ! Vajrasattva himself is now established within your heart;
he would depart at that very moment, piercing through [your chest], if you were to speak this method to another.
Having thus commanded: "This water of hell shall burn you for transgressing the pledge; through the preservation of the pledge comes accomplishment. Drink this vajra-amṛta water! Thus [he spoke].

Having recited [the mantra] and caused [the disciple] to drink from the vessel, he should say: "From this day forward, I am Vajrapāṇi to you; whatever I tell you to do, that must be performed by you, and you must not disregard me. Lest, by failing to avoid misfortune, you should meet your end and fall into hell. This is the procedure for giving the water of the pledge (*samaya*). ||5||

Thereafter, immediately following emptiness (*śūnyatā*), having manifested the form of Amitābha born from the syllable *ĀḤ*, one should recite: "May all the Tathāgatas empower [me]; may Vajrasattva enter into me. Then, one should visualize: in his heart, upon a yellow square earth-maṇḍala marked with a vajra and born from *Laṃ*, on a sun disc is a blue *Hūṃ*. On the head, within a white circular water-maṇḍala marked by a vase and born from *Vaṃ*, on a moon disc is a white syllable *Haḥ*. In the throat, within a blue wind-maṇḍala resembling a bow and marked by two fluttering banners, born from the syllable *Yaṃ*, on a moon disc is a red syllable *Āḥ*. Having summoned the Mind-Vajra, Body-Vajra, and Speech-Vajra by means of light rays from the seed-syllable in one's own heart, they are absorbed respectively into the *Hūṃ*, *Haḥ*, and *Āḥ* syllables which constitute their essential nature. Below the feet, ignited by the wind-maṇḍala, is a red triangular fire-maṇḍala marked with the letter *Raṃ* and radiating rays of light. One should meditate that the disciple is being lifted up by the red syllable *Ṛḥ* situated there, while his entire body is filled by masses of light rays from the syllable *Ṛḥ* entering through the openings of the feet, as well as by the light rays from the *Hūṃ* and other syllables. While scattering incense and ringing a bell, one should repeat the mantra one hundred times: *Āveśaya stabhaya rararara cālāya oṃ hūṃ haḥ āḥ ṛḥ*.

One intent on meditation should cause [the disciple] to enter [possession], saying: *tiṣṭha krodhāveśaya hūṃ śrīherukāya viṭmahāvidyārājāya śrīmahe svāhā*. If he has entered possession, he leaps far upward. Then, having meditated upon Mount Meru made of vajra above him, above that the Maheśvara-maṇḍala, above that a yellow five-pronged vajra, above that the syllable *yaḥ*, and above that Vairocana, one should cause him to turn back from that state. While such possession exists, the seed-syllable of the Mind-Vajra, being impelled by the rays of light from the seed-syllables, moves toward the Speech-Vajra which consists of the seed-syllable; and having visualized a red syllable *āḥ* on the tongue, situated upon a moon and surrounded by garlands of flames, one should say, "Speak, O Vajra! Thus he will speak of what is auspicious or inauspicious for himself or for another. Thereafter, having drawn the deity who has descended through the rays of light from his own heart and causing her to merge with the seed-syllables in his own heart, one should hold a vajra at the head of the disciple and dismiss [the deity] with the mantra *oṃ kṛto vaḥ sarvasattvārtha...* and so forth, followed by *hūṃ haḥ āḥ ṛḥ mur*. This is the procedure for possession. 6.

Then, having asked the disciple facing the mandala, "What kind of appearance do you perceive before your eyes?", [the teacher determines] the accomplishment of pacification, enrichment, subjugation, or malevolent rites according to the white, yellow, red, or black appearances reported by him respectively.
Then [he recites]: "This disciple has been properly initiated into the mandala by me;
according to his merit, let there be for him the lineage of the deities."
Whatever view he may have, in whichever lineage he stands,
and whatever the power of his merit may be— may it all be such within this mandala.
Thus ends the procedure for the entry of the blindfolded disciple. 7.

Then, with the syllable *trāṃ*, one performs the supreme recitation over dūrvā grass and fruit. One offers it with: *oṃ tiṣṭha vajra dṛḍho me bhava śāśvato me bhava hṛdayaṃ me 'dhitiṣṭha sarvasiddhiṃ me prayaccha hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ āḥ khaṃ vīra hūṃ pratīccha kusumañjali nātha hoḥ*.
This is the ritual for the casting of the flower (*puṣpapātana*). ||8||

Reciting "Oṃ, accept this being, O you of great strength," [one performs] the casting of flowers, the offering of *dūrvā* grass and fruit, and the bathing with water. Thus is the consecration with the garland (*mālābhiṣeka*). ||9||
Thereafter, having visualized the master of the disciple as a moon in the heart, the letter *ra* on the forehead, and the two eyes as blazing with fire,
[one recites]: "Vajrasattva himself, intent today upon opening your eyes,
opens all your eyes with the unsurpassed Vajra-eye."
Oṃ jñānacakṣuḥ hūṃ aḥ svāhā! Remove the blindfold; behold Hevajra!
Behold this maṇḍala now with the force of faith.
You have been born into the family of the Buddhas and are empowered by mudrās and mantras.
Through this perfection, you shall become the foremost of all accomplishments and the supreme of commitments;
perform the worship of the mantras with the graceful union of the vajra and the lotus.
I have entered the great mandala of the Vajra-mandala;
I have been shown the great mandala of the Yoga-mandala; I have been initiated into the great mandala of the Guhya-mandala.
One should cause [the disciple] to recite "hoḥ hoḥ hoḥ. This is the procedure for the disciple’s entry into the maṇḍala consisting of the act of seeing it. ||10||
Thereafter, for the purpose of the water consecration, with knees placed upon the ground and palms joined in *añjali*, [one should pray]:
"Just as the Great Festival was bestowed by Bodhivajra upon the Buddhas,
so too, for the sake of my protection, grant me today the Sky-Vajra and the rest."

Then follows the formal request (*adhyeṣaṇā*). Having visualized the disciple in the form of Vajradhara, the rite of waving the lamps (*nīrājana*) is performed. Subsequently, having worshipped the Tathāgatas residing in the infinite directions and the Knowledge Goddesses (*vidyādevī*) with rays of light from the seed-syllable in one’s heart for the sake of the disciple’s consecration:
“The Buddhas, for the protection of the world, were consecrated by the Holder of the Vajra;
just as Guṇākara was given [consecration], so indeed grant it to this one.”

Having thus supplicated with this verse, those Tathāgatas, endowed with wisdom, melt through great passion (*mahārāga*). Entering within through the door of Vairocana, they emerge via the path of the *vajra*. That disciple is then introduced by the Goddess through the mouth of her lotus. Instantly, following the state of emptiness, [the disciple] is consecrated as the form of Akṣobhya together with Prajñā, born from the syllable *HŪṂ* and inseparable from the Jñānasattva. Then, emerging from the lotus with their bodies complete in arms, faces, and so forth, having filled the path of departure, they remain accompanied by the Vidyās such as Locanā and the rest. With umbrellas, banners, flags, garments, musical instruments, songs, dances, showers of flowers, saffron, and the like; with white flasks filled with the nectar of bodhicitta held in bud-like hands; and with the Goddesses such as Rūpavajrā and the others, they consecrate that disciple who has emerged from the lotus. "Whatever auspiciousness belongs to the Great Bliss, the Lord of all families, the essence of all, who dwells in the hearts of all sentient beings and is the progenitor of all beings—may that auspiciousness be yours in the supreme consecration (*paramābhiṣeka*). Oṃ, I consecrate you with the consecration of Mahāsukha-Vajrasattva. May you become firm in the sovereignty over all Tathāgatas. This is the consecration.

I bestow the great vajra, honored by the three realms, which arises from the abode of the three secrets of all Buddhas. Oṃ āḥ, consecrate with the vajra-water hūṃ; I am you, O Surata. This is the ritual for the water consecration. ||11||

Then, one should visualize the Guru, who has been requested with the words beginning "O Bodhivajra," as Śrī Ratnasambhava, unified with the Jñānasattva, being consecrated by the Tathāgata goddesses in the sky with vases, while Rūpavajrā and the others offer auspicious songs. The consecration is as before. Then, the Ratnasambhava-vajra is the Vajra of that same nature, in the form of the Jñānasattva. One should visualize the crown empowered by the five Tathāgatas, who are the lords of the families of the disciple situated in the center, [placed] respectively upon the middle of his head, the forehead, the two sides, the crown, and the back, with the mantras: Oṃ vajradhātvīśvari abhiṣiñca hūṃ | Oṃ sattvavajri abhiṣiñca bhrūṃ | Oṃ ratnavajri abhiṣiñca āḥ | Oṃ dharmavajri abhiṣiñca hrīḥ | Oṃ karmavajri abhiṣiñca trāṃ | "Consecration is the great vajra... and so forth, ending with: "Oṃ āḥ, consecrate me with the vajra-crown, hūṃ; you are Surata, and I am he. Oṃ vajratuṣṭāḥ. This is the procedure for the crown consecration. ||12||
Thereafter, one should bind a turban on the forehead with the mantra "Oṃ hūṃ trāṃ hrīḥ aḥ. This is the procedure for the cloth-consecration (paṭābhiṣeka). ||13||

Then, having visualized the disciple who has spoken thus as the transformation of the lotus, Amitābha in form, inseparable from the Jñānasattva, and the vajra as being of the nature of Amitābha, [the master says]: "Abhiṣekam... and so forth:
"Today you are consecrated by the Buddhas through the vajra-consecration. Take this, which is the state of all the Buddhas, the vajra for the sake of perfect accomplishment."
Having touched the disciple’s heart, throat, and head with the vajra, one should place it in his right hand. This is the procedure for the vajra empowerment (vajrābhiṣeka). ||14||

Thereafter, having visualized the sky as the nature of Amoghasiddhi, inseparable from the wisdom-being (jñānasattva) in response to that request, and having visualized the bell as the transformation of Amoghasiddhi; [reciting] "The consecration," and so forth, one places it in his left hand. Then, with hands joined by the vajra and the vajra-bell, one causes him to perform the gesture of embracing the mudrā.

Having recited: "Oṃ, I consecrate you as the Lord of Vajras; remain, you who are the Vajra-samaya," one should cause [the disciple] to recite: "Oṃ vajraghaṇṭā aḥ aḥ, O Blessed One, you have been grasped by me; be present. This is the procedure for the bell-consecration (ghaṇṭābhiṣeka). ||15||

Thereafter, having visualized that [disciple] who has thus requested [initiation] as the wisdom-being (*jñānasattva*) of one flavor with Vairocana born from the *oṃ* syllable and the wheel, and while bestowing upon him the vajra and bell at his head, [the master says]: "Oṃ, Vajrasattva, I initiate you by means of the vajra-name initiation as Dveṣavajrasattva," and so forth. This is the procedure for the name initiation. (16)
Then, to that disciple who has offered the ritual fee and joined his palms in reverence, [the master says]:
"O treasure of compassion, grant me the Vajrācārya initiation,
so that by your grace I may become capable of accomplishing the welfare of both myself and others."

Having recited this, [the disciple] has made a request to the Guru. [The Guru], whose nature is the form of Vajrasattva, [performs] the water initiation according to the procedure described [above]. The sequence of visualization and the *nīrājana* offering is as before. From the seed-syllable in the heart until the descent from the tip of the vajra, [one performs] the initiation, etc., with the mantra: *Oṃ āḥ sarvatathāgatābhiṣekasamaśriye hūṃ svāhā*. Then, having visualized Akṣobhya upon the crown, and having likewise visualized the other Tathāgatas and goddesses there, one meditates on that vajra as the form of Vajrasattva, marked by *Hūṃ Jaṃ*:
"The Being without beginning or end is Vajrasattva, the Great Joy."
Samantabhadra is the self of all; he is the Lord of Vajragarvā, the Lord.
"The Blessed One is the Primordial Being. Reciting thus, one should cause [the disciple] to grasp it as reality and as praise. This is the Vajra-samaya. ||17||
Then, having visualized the bell as arising from the syllable ĀḤ:
"This is the bell of all Buddhas, known to follow the resonance of sound; for you too, O Master, it is considered by those who strive for supreme enlightenment to be the essence of right conduct."
Reciting this three times according to the true principle, one should cause [the disciple] to grasp it:
"Existence is indeed pure by its very nature, yet it is made manifest through various natures;
by beings who are pure by nature, the supreme manifestation is brought forth."
Thus is the commitment of the bell. ||18||
"Samaya is said to be the mudrās because of the firmness of the mental form;
since all mudrās are made firm by it, it is therefore proclaimed as 'mudrā'. Thus [it is said].
"Having empowered the wisdom-seal (*jñānamudrā*) through the enjoyment of all desires, accomplish all goals and attainments by means of the seal's extreme firmness. Thus it is said.
Embracing is the commitment (*samaya*) of the mudrā. Thus is the procedure for bestowing the three commitments. ||19||
"Embracing with both hands a Prajñā of sixteen years, through the union of the bell and the vajra, this is considered the initiation of the Ācārya. Thus it is said.
The purification of the reality of the mandala and so forth; the procedure for the master’s initiation, also known as the irreversible initiation. ||20||

Then, having himself recited the Heart-mantra and other mantras one hundred and eight times or three times, he should give them to the disciple while saying: "O Blessed One, you have been given by me; be present within this [disciple]. The disciple should also say: "O Blessed One, you have been received by me; be present within me," and should recite it three times. This is the procedure for the offering of the Yantra. ||21||
Then, having meditated on the syllable *praṃ* at the eyes of the disciple: *Oṃ vajranetrā prahara paṭalaṃ hrīḥ!
O child, the veil of ignorance has been removed from you by the Victors, just as the film of cataracts was removed from the world by the King of Physicians with his surgical probes.*
Thus ends the procedure for the application of collyrium. ||22||
Then, taking up a mirror, he should show it to the disciple while it has been consecrated with the syllable *ĀḤ*. "All phenomena are like reflections; they are transparent, pure, and unclouded;
they are ungraspable and inexpressible, arising from causes and karma."
Like a mirror, O Vajrasattva, you are clear, pure, and indeed untroubled;
the Lord of all Buddhas himself abides within your heart, my child.
Having thus understood that all phenomena are without intrinsic nature and without abode,
perform incomparable benefit for sentient beings, for you have been born from the breast of the Protectors.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the consecration of the mirror. ||23||

Then, having recited "Hoḥ" and offered [the arrow], he should say: "Oṃ, cause all the Tathāgatas to be impassioned. The disciple should also say: "I cause all the Tathāgatas to be impassioned. This is the procedure for the casting of the arrow. ||24||
Then the disciple, having offered his own wisdom to the guru for the sake of the secret initiation, and with palms joined in reverence, should conceive of the guru as Vajrasattva, saying:
"By the grace of your feet, I have attained the unsurpassed practice;
therefore, O Protector, grant me favor by means of the secret initiation."

One should request [the initiation] with a verse. Then the Guru, possessing the ego-identity of the Lord of the Mandala (*cakreśāhaṃkāra*), having first performed the purification of the vajra and lotus with that consort—who has assumed the form of a goddess immediately after the emptiness of ordinary man and woman—enters into meditative union (*samāpatti*).

Reciting: *Oṃ, I am of the nature of the Vajra of the Passion of all Tathāgatas*, one then visualizes that the Tathāgatas, such as Vairocana and others, who have entered into Locanā and the other goddesses by means of the rays from the seed-syllable in one’s own heart, enter into oneself through the gate of Vairocana. Having contemplated that they melt through great passion and emerge via the *avadhūtī* channel, one stabilizes the innate [bliss] within the vajra-jewel. Pressing the jewel with the thumb and ring finger, one draws it up from the lotus. Imagining that this fluid of the Tathāgata is inseparable from one’s own bodhicitta, one conceives of it in the form of the Speech-Vajra (*vāgvajra*). Out of fear that the disciple might lack faith upon seeing it, one binds them with a blindfold so that it remains beyond the range of their vision.
Just as the sons of the Buddha were sprinkled by the past Vajradharas and others,
so do I sprinkle you, my child, with the beautiful mind of awakening (bodhicitta).

Thus, reciting the mantra of the Lord of the Maṇḍala, he should cause [the drop] to fall. He too, with the realization that it is the assembly of all Tathāgatas such as Vairocana, should drink while saying, "Aho! Great Bliss! Then the Wisdom Consort (Prajñā), having risen and being naked, should place the drop of nectar—the Tathāgata residing in her own lotus—into his mouth. He too should drink in that manner. This is the procedure for the Secret Empowerment. ||25||
Thereafter, when the disciple has made this request with the words "O Bodhivajra," and so forth:
"This delightful dhāraṇī of yours, ordained by the Buddhas, should be cultivated;
through the application of the sequence of the wheel, experience the sublime bliss."

"Observing the mind within the jewel from the vajra-paryaṅka posture"—having thus instructed, he should offer [the consort]. She too, showing the disciple a lotus free of stains and made fragrant with saffron and other scents, says:
"Aho! My lotus is endowed with all bliss."
I stand before him who serves according to the prescribed rule.
O Padmā, perform whatever task is required, such as the sādhana of the Perfect Buddha;
for the King of Great Bliss himself is always established right here.

"Enjoy me! May liberation arise! Thus he should say. He too, being himself the form of the deity, having manifested Prajñā in the form of the Goddess, visualizes the stamens and gem of the lotus and thunderbolt produced by *hrīḥ* and *hūṃ*, and the yellow syllable *phaṭ* within the vajra-mouth produced by *āḥ* and *oṃ*. With the left-hand channel situated at the tip, marked by the red syllable *hrīḥ*, he moves it with the forefinger and the tongue while making the sound *śīṭ*. Reciting the mantra: *oṃ śī ha3 svāhā*, he thinks: "Through the passion of all the Tathāgatas, I am of the nature of the Vajra. Thus he repeats the mantra.

Through the instruction of the Guru, the distinction between bliss is understood. Having drawn in the Tathāgatas and others with rays from the seed-syllable in one’s own heart, and having been entered by the Guru, one becomes of one flavor with Śrī Vairocana, Locanā, and the rest; thus one should begin the rati. Through contact with Prajñā, the glorious one should perceive reality (tattva), while observing the mind within the jewel [of the crown] from the vajra-paryaṅka posture.
Having thus visualized—this is the procedure for the initiation of the knowledge of Prajñā. ||26||

Immediately thereafter, one should bestow the fourth consecration. One should explain that very fourth consecration as follows: it is the sprouted *bodhicitta* of the wisdom of insight (*prajñājñāna*), which, increasing through meditative cultivation, has attained freedom from obscuration; it is reality (*tattva*), the intrinsic nature of the inconceivability of all phenomena, possessing the seven limbs, having the nature of the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*), and being the essence of the Great Vajra Holder. Thus ends the procedure for the fourth consecration. ||27||

Immediately thereafter, having placed his hand upon the hand of that Prajñā, and holding both with his own left hand, he places his right hand, which holds a vajra, upon the head of the disciple, making the Tathāgatas witnesses: "O witnesses of the ripening [of karma], you are here; she has been entrusted by me to him. There is no other means for Buddhahood, and these three worlds are pure;
therefore, never cause her to be separated from this one."
This is the unsurpassed vow of knowledge (vidyāvrata) of all the Buddhas;
the fool who transgresses it shall not attain supreme accomplishment.
Saying this, he should bestow the vow of knowledge (*vidyāvrata*). This is the procedure for the bestowal of the vow of knowledge. ||28||
Thereafter, having visualized the disciple in the form of Vajrasattva:
"This state of all buddhahood resides in the hand of Vajrasattva;
you too, O Vajrapāṇi, firm in your vow, must always hold it fast. Thus.

While reciting, he should cause [the disciple] to grasp the vajra. He should grasp it while reciting: "Oṃ, O Vajrasattva, abide in this vajra-samaya, the accomplishment of all Tathāgatas; I hold you fast! Hīḥ hi hi hi hi hūṃ. Thus ends the ritual procedure for the vajra-vow. ||29||

Then, having visualized the disciple in the form of Saṃvara and the woman in the form of Vajravārāhī, one causes the wisdom deity— invoked by rays from the seed-syllable in one’s own heart— to enter [them]. Akṣobhya in the form of a wheel, Amitābha as the nature of earrings, Ratneśa in the neck-garland, and Vairocana is said to be in the hand.
Because it is stated that Amogha resides in the girdle, [the sequence] is as follows.

Having instantly visualized the wheel, earrings, necklace, bracelets, and girdle as the forms of Akṣobhya, Amitābha, Ratnasaṃbhava, Vairocana, Amoghasiddhi, and so forth; having caused the Jñānasattva to enter there in that same manner; and having resolved with conviction that the mudrās—the wheel and the rest—which have been transformed from Akṣobhya and the others, are themselves the very nature of Akṣobhya and the others. *Pāṁ āṁ jñāṁ khaṁ hūṁ* (for the offering of water). *Puṁ paṁ lāṁ ghaṁ* (for the offering of flowers). *Stute* (praise). Recite the mantra for the *jāpa* and the *bali*. Then the ornaments. *Dhara 2* (for the song). With the mantra: *Oṃ śrīvajra he he ru ru ka hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ ḍākinījālasaṃvaraṃ svāhā*, recited three times. *Vibhūti* (ashes). With the mantra: *Oṃ sarvabuddha-ḍākinīye vajravarṇanīye vajravairocanīye hūṃ phaṭ 3 svāhā*, recited three times. *Vyāghracarma* (tiger skin). With the mantra: *Oṃ dhara 2 dhāraya 2 mardaya 2 vajradhṛka hūṃ phaṭ svāhā*, and *Oṃ vajravairocanīye hūṃ 2 phaṭ svāhā*, recited three times. Place the wheel on the head.
O hero Dattamanas, take up the discus whose nature is Akṣobhya;
this is the seal (mudrā) of Śrī Vajrasattva, abiding both externally and internally. (1)

Oṃ vajradharma samayas tvaṃ kuru 2 ārolika hūṃ phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ hrīḥ ha ha hūṃ 2 phaṭ—this is recited three times. Two earrings [are placed] on the two ears: "Take this given ear-ring, O hero, whose nature is Amitābha! This is the seal of Śrī Vajrasattva, abiding externally and internally. (2)

Oṃ vajrasūryatamovidhūnan samayaḥ tvaṃ ratnadhṛk hūṃ phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ sarvabuddha-ḍākinīye, etc. (Thus) recited three times. [The necklace] on the neck: "Take this necklace, O hero of subdued mind, which is of the nature of Ratnasambhava. This is the mudrā of Śrī Vajrasattva, abiding both externally and internally. (3)

Oṃ śāśvata paramaśāśvata ehyehi jinajik hūṃ phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ haḥ nama hi svāhā hūṃ vauṣaṭ he hūṃ hūṃ hoḥ phaṭ 2 haṃ. (Recite this three times. Two bracelets, like rings on the hands: "O Hero, accept this bracelet of eternal nature that has been offered. This is the seal of Śrī Vajrasattva, abiding both externally and internally. (4)

Oṃ hūṃ hrīḥ prajñādhṛk hūṃ phaṭ svāhā | Oṃ vaṃ hāṃ yāṃ hrīṃ māṃ hraṃ hrīṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ | Thus, recite three times. [Place] the girdle on the hips. "Take this girdle, O hero whose mind is focused; it is of the nature of Amoghasiddhi. This is the mudrā of Śrī Vajrasattva, abiding both externally and internally. (5)

*Oṃ śrīvajra he he ru ru kaṃ hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ ḍākinījālasaṃvaraṃ svāhā.* Thus, the two mantras are recited three times each. With the root mantra of Śrī Saṃvara, the *brahmasūtra*, the necklace (*hāra*) suspended from the neck, the ornaments, the vajra, the garland of severed heads (*muṇḍamālā*), and so forth, are each consecrated three times as being the very nature of their respective deities in their respective places. With the thirty-six mantras beginning with *Oṃ pracaṇḍe hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ* and ending with *Oṃ rūpiṇīye hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ*, the vessel for drinking the nectar of gnosis (*jñānamṛtapāna*) is consecrated three times in the hand. As for the *khaṭvāṅga* and the hand-drum (*ḍamaru*), they are consecrated three times with the root mantra of the Blessed One.
"O Hero, take this granted khaṭvāṅga, ḍamaru, and vessel;
this is the mudrā of Śrī Vajrasattva, abiding both externally and internally. Reciting this, he should cause [the disciple] to take them.

Thereafter, having taken a flower garland, one should recite the root mantra one hundred and eight times. [Then follow: worship with flowers and so forth, praise, the bali offering, the pledge (samaya), the circumambulation and bali offering, and the ritual for the conduct vow (caryāvratavidhi). ||30||

Then, while the Tathāgata was thus [visualized], one should perform the conduct of Māra: placing the left fist, with the robe-cuff held within it, against the heart, and with the right hand in the *abhaya* (fear-dispelling) mudrā, recite:
Oṃ! Here I am; Vajrasattva, the Tathāgata, prophesies for you, having extracted you from the miserable states of existence, for the sake of the ultimate pacification of cyclic existence.

Reciting the mantra "O Amukavajra Tathāgata, may you attain siddhi; you are the pledge (samaya) of bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ," he should grant the prophecy. One who is thus prophesied should have faith that he has been prophesied for perfect enlightenment by all the Tathāgatas. This is the procedure for the prophecy. ||31||

Thereafter, reciting "Bhṛṃ Jaṃ Dharmacakraṃ Oṃ Vajrahetumaṃ," [he places] it in the right hand. Reciting "Āḥkārajaṃ Śaṃ Khaṃ Oṃ Vajrabhāṣa Raṃ," [he places] a book born from the first vowel in the left hand. Reciting the first vowel, he gives a bell born from the final vowel while ringing that bell, reciting the final vowel:
"Everything has the characteristic of space, and space itself is without characteristics.
Through union with the equality of space, the equality of all things is clearly manifest."
From this day forward, by the mere arising of the innate thought of awakening, turn the wheel of Dharma;
for you shall completely fill the unsurpassed conch of Dharma in every direction.
Thus he should say:
"For the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, throughout all worlds and in every way,
turn the wheel of Dharma according to the needs of those to be trained."
"O you whose very nature is wisdom and skillful means, like a supreme wish-fulfilling gem, untiring and free from attachment, now act for the benefit of sentient beings. Thus it is said.

Regarding "reciting": by substituting the words *vajra*, *ratna*, *padma*, *karma*, and *cakra* in place of the word *dharma*, one should grant permission through these five recitations. Having prostrated, he should say: "I shall do exactly as the Lord commands. This is the procedure for granting permission. ||32||
Holding a parasol over his head and having performed a circumambulation,
he should speak while scattering a handful of flowers together with the parasol at the entrance of the mandala.
"This disciple, having been thus informed, shall become a holder of the tantra.
Having said this, he should set aside the parasol belonging to the Lord of the Mandala elsewhere.
He should speak so as to be taken to heart by the disciple:
"Now you are a master of the mandala, a holder of the mantra-tantras,
and one esteemed by the Buddhas, the Bodhisattvas, and the deities."
Out of compassion for sentient beings, you should diligently draw the maṇḍala according to the ritual procedure, and practitioners should be engaged in accordance with the tantra.
Having seen and entered this supreme, most secret, and excellent maṇḍala,
you are today liberated from all sins and well-established.
There is no further falling away for you from this vehicle of great bliss;
your suffering of existence has ceased for the sake of the ultimate accomplishment of liberation.
Today you, O Venerable One, have been consecrated by all the Buddhas together with the Holders of the Vajra;
it is certain that you are the Lord, the Great King of the Three Realms.
There is no evil in the three realms equal to dispassion, nor is there any merit [equal to passion];
therefore, you must never again practice detachment from sensual desires.
"Enjoy all sensual pleasures without fear from any quarter;
the nectar of the five meats is to be consumed, for this is the observance other than that of a Rākṣasa."
One must not commit the taking of life, nor should one abandon a jewel of a woman;
one must not forsake one's teacher, for the vow is difficult to transgress.
There is nothing that cannot be accomplished by a mind endowed with wisdom and skillful means;
do not fear, for there is no sin in you, according to the word of the Tathāgata.

Thus, act! You have attained the state of Vajrasattva—eternal and peerless in this world of fleeting pleasures—having now realized your own samaya, the diamond of mental clarity, which bestows inexhaustible bliss. Furthermore, this is the nature of reality (*dharmatā*): just as one who has been consecrated according to the ritual is protected for their welfare by all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas with minds full of affection, like a beloved son. This is the procedure for consolation. ||33||
And the disciple, having thus received the empowerment, being confident and joyful, thinks: "I shall do this.
Today my birth has become fruitful, and my life has become fruitful.
Today I am born into the family of the Buddhas; I am now a son of the Buddha."
Thus he should say.
He should give the sacrificial fee and so forth to the guru.
Thus the ritual procedure for consecration is completed.
